{{Short description|Mathematical plane curve}}
{{CS1 config|mode=cs1}}
[[Image:NegativePedal.gif|500px|right|thumb|[[Circle]] — negative pedal curve of a [[limaçon]]]]
In [[geometry]], a '''negative pedal curve''' is a [[plane curve]] that can be constructed from another plane curve ''C'' and a fixed point ''P''. For each point ''X''&nbsp;≠&nbsp;''P'' on the curve ''C'', the negative pedal curve has a [[tangent]] that passes through ''X'' and is [[perpendicular]] to line ''XP''.  Constructing the negative pedal curve is the [[inverse operation]] to constructing a [[pedal curve]].

==Definition==
In the plane, for every point ''X'' other than ''P'' there is a unique line through ''X'' perpendicular to ''XP''. For a given curve in the plane and a given fixed point ''P'', called the '''pedal point''', the '''negative pedal curve''' is the [[envelope (mathematics)|envelope]] of the lines ''XP'' for which ''X'' lies on the given curve.<ref name=":0">{{cite book |contribution=Negative Pedals |date=2010 |title=Book of Curves |pages=157–160 |editor-last=Lockwood |editor-first=E. H. |orig-date=1961 |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/book-of-curves/negative-pedals/3F3257272309E7A6385D790253604A28 |access-date=2025-06-10 |place=Cambridge |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-04444-8}}</ref>

==Parameterization==
For a parametrically defined curve, its negative pedal curve with pedal point (0; 0) is defined as:<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Negative Pedal Curve |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/NegativePedalCurve.html |access-date=2025-06-10 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
:<math>X[x,y]=\frac{(y^2-x^2)y'+2xyx'}{xy'-yx'}</math>

:<math>Y[x,y]=\frac{(x^2-y^2)x'+2xyy'}{xy'-yx'}</math>

== Examples ==
The negative pedal curve of a [[Line (geometry)|line]] is a parabola. The negative pedal curves of a [[circle]] are an [[ellipse]] if ''P'' is chosen to be inside the circle, and a [[hyperbola]] if ''P'' is chosen to be outside the circle.<ref name=":0" /> The negative pedal curve of a [[parabola]] with respect to its focus is the [[Tschirnhausen cubic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Curves/Tschirnhaus/|title=Tschirnhaus' Cubic|work=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]]|access-date=2025-10-02}}</ref>

==Properties==
The negative pedal curve of a [[pedal curve]] with the same pedal point is the original curve.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Edwards |first=Joseph |url=http://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.109607 |title=An Elementary Treatise On The Differential Calculus |date=1892 |edition=2nd |pages=165 |language=en}}</ref>

==See also==
